European Roots

Headquartered in the Heart of Europe

From Paris to Milan, EuroFiducia connects investors across France and Italy to global markets. Our platform reflects the elegance and reliability of European financial traditions, combined with modern technology for seamless investing.

🇫🇷 Paris 🇮🇹 Milan 🇪🇺 Brussels

How It Works

Get started with EuroFiducia in four simple steps — from account creation to your first investment.

1

Create Your Account

Register in minutes with our secure 5-step verification process. Open to investors in France, Italy, and across Europe.

2

Verify Your Identity

Complete KYC/AML verification with your ID and proof of address. Required by EU regulations for all financial accounts.

3

Fund Your Account

Deposit via SEPA bank transfer, credit/debit card, or cryptocurrency. Minimum first deposit is €100. Funds credited within 1-2 business days.

4

Start Investing

Choose from 12 asset classes, pre-built portfolios, or apply for a loan. Track performance in real-time from your dashboard.

Security & Client Fund Protection

Your investments are protected by multiple layers of security and regulatory oversight.

🏛

Regulated & Authorized

EuroFiducia operates under EU MiFID II framework with oversight from French ACPR/AMF and Italian CONSOB regulators.

🔒

Segregated Client Accounts

Client funds are held in segregated accounts at tier-1 European banks, completely separate from company operating funds.

🛡

Bank-Grade Encryption

256-bit SSL/TLS encryption, two-factor authentication, and continuous security monitoring protect every transaction.

🚨

Investor Protection Scheme

Eligible client assets are covered by European investor protection schemes up to €100,000 per investor.

Our Mission

EuroFiducia was founded with a clear vision: to democratize access to professional-grade investment products for savers and investors across France and Italy. For too long, sophisticated portfolios combining European government bonds, real estate, private equity, and global equities were reserved for the wealthy few. We changed that.

By combining institutional-grade asset management with an intuitive, fully multilingual digital platform, EuroFiducia empowers every investor — from the cautious saver building a Livret A habit to the ambitious growth-seeker diversifying across global markets — to build wealth on their own terms, in their own language.

Our Values

🛡️

Security First

Bank-grade encryption, segregated client accounts, and full regulatory compliance protect every euro you invest.

🌍

Multilingual by Design

Every user experiences the platform in their native language — French, Italian, and eight more — while our team operates seamlessly behind the scenes.

⚖️

Transparency

Clear fees, honest risk disclosures, and undeniable transaction receipts. No hidden costs, no surprises.

🤖

AI-Powered Support

Our AI assistant handles common questions instantly in your language, with seamless escalation to human experts when needed.

📈

Performance

Professionally managed portfolios targeting consistent returns across conservative, balanced, and growth strategies.

🤝

Client-Centric

Personal messaging, dedicated support, and tools designed around how you actually manage your money.

Rooted in European Financial Heritage

Headquartered in the heart of Paris, with offices in Milan and Rome, EuroFiducia draws on centuries of European financial tradition. Our approach blends the prudence of French banking heritage with the entrepreneurial energy of Italian markets.

From the Banque de France's legacy of monetary stability to the Borsa Italiana's dynamic equity culture, we bring the best of both nations to your portfolio.

How to Apply in 4 Steps

From application to disbursement — a streamlined process with full visibility.

1

Create Account

Register and complete bank account verification with IBAN, BIC, and identity details.

2

Choose Loan

Select the loan type, amount, and repayment term that fits your needs.

3

Submit Application

Your application is reviewed by our team. You'll receive email and SMS updates at every stage.

4

Get Funded

Upon approval, funds are disbursed to your verified bank account within 3–5 business days.

Who Can Apply

Eligibility Requirements

Open to residents of France, Italy, and across the European Union.

✅ Basic Eligibility

  • Age 18 or older with valid government-issued ID
  • Resident of France, Italy, or an EU member state
  • Verified bank account with IBAN and BIC/SWIFT
  • Proof of stable income or revenue (for business loans)
  • Completed KYC/AML verification

📄 Required Documents

  • National ID card or passport
  • Proof of address (utility bill or bank statement, <3 months old)
  • Recent payslips or tax return (last 2–3 months)
  • Bank statements showing income deposits
  • Property documents (for mortgage & home equity loans)
Frequently Asked Questions

Loan Questions Answered

What is the minimum and maximum loan amount?▾
Loan amounts vary by type. Personal loans start from €1,000 up to €50,000. Mortgages range from €50,000 to €1,000,000. Business loans can go up to €500,000. Exact limits are shown on each loan type's detail card above.
How long does approval take?▾
For personal and auto loans, preliminary approval can be received within 24–48 hours. Mortgages and business loans may take 5–10 business days due to additional documentation and property/business valuation. You will receive email and SMS notifications at each stage.
Can I apply if I live outside France or Italy?▾
Yes. EuroFiducia serves residents across the European Union. You must have a verified bank account with a valid IBAN. Some loan products may have country-specific conditions based on local regulations.
Are there early repayment penalties?▾
Most of our loan products allow early or partial repayment without penalties, in compliance with European consumer protection regulations. Mortgage early repayment terms may vary — full details are provided in your loan agreement.
How are interest rates determined?▾
Interest rates are based on the loan type, amount, term, your credit profile, and prevailing European Central Bank rates. Fixed and variable rate options are available. Your personalized rate is presented during the application process.
Will I be notified about my application status?▾
Absolutely. You will receive notifications via email, your EuroFiducia dashboard, and SMS (if opted in) at every stage: submission received, under review, approved/rejected, and funds disbursed. Our admin team is also notified of all activity.

Ready to Apply for a Loan?

Create your EuroFiducia account today, complete bank verification, and apply for the loan that fits your needs. Our team will guide you through every step.

Terms of Service

The terms governing your use of EuroFiducia's investment platform

Last updated: January 2024 · France 🇫🇷 & Italy 🇮🇹

Contents

  • 1. Acceptance of Terms
  • 2. Definitions
  • 3. Eligibility

1. Acceptance of Terms

Welcome to EuroFiducia ("we", "us", "our", the "Platform"). By accessing or using our website, mobile interface, and investment services, you ("you", the "User") agree to be bound by these Terms of Service ("Terms"). If you do not agree to these Terms, you must not access or use the Platform.

These Terms constitute a legally binding agreement between you and EuroFiducia SAS, a company registered in France, providing cross-border investment services to residents of France and Italy under applicable European regulations.

2. Definitions

  • Platform — the EuroFiducia digital investment marketplace accessible via website and mobile interface.
  • Account — your personal investment account opened after successful registration and verification.
  • Portfolio — a managed investment strategy (Conservative, Balanced, Growth, Euro Growth, or Global Growth).
  • Transaction — any deposit, withdrawal, investment purchase, sale, or transfer recorded on your account.
  • Receipt — the official confirmation document generated for each transaction.
  • KYC — Know Your Customer verification process required by anti-money-laundering regulations.

3. Eligibility

You must be at least 18 years of age and a legal resident of France or Italy (or an eligible European jurisdiction) to open an account. You must have the legal capacity to enter into binding contracts. By registering, you confirm that you are not legally prohibited from using investment services and that you are not acting on behalf of a person so prohibited.

4. Account Registration

To open an account, you must complete our four-step registration process: (1) Account details, (2) Identity/KYC verification, (3) Investor profile assessment, and (4) Compliance declarations. You agree to provide accurate, current, and complete information and to update such information to keep it accurate.

You are responsible for safeguarding your password and for all activity conducted under your account. You must notify us immediately of any unauthorized use of your account. You may reset your login credentials at any time through the password reset facility.

5. KYC & Verification

As a regulated investment platform, we are required by European AML directives (AMLD5/AMLD6) and national regulations (AMF in France, CONSOB in Italy) to verify your identity before activating your account. You must provide a valid government-issued identification document, proof of address, and such additional information as we may reasonably require.

We reserve the right to suspend or close accounts where verification cannot be completed or where information provided is found to be inaccurate, misleading, or fraudulent.

6. Deposits & Withdrawals

You may fund your account via SEPA bank transfer, debit/credit card, or open banking. All deposits are credited to your segregated client account and are available for investment once cleared. Withdrawals are processed to your verified bank account and may be subject to compliance review.

We aim to process withdrawals within 2–5 business days depending on the method and compliance checks. Each deposit and withdrawal generates an official receipt with full transaction details, reference numbers, and processing codes.

7. Investments & Risk

Investments available on the Platform include stocks, ETFs, bonds (OAT, BTP), real estate (SCPI), sustainable/ESG funds, private equity, commodities, cryptoassets, retirement products (PER, pension), and cash/savings products (Livret A, LDDS).

Risk Warning: All investments carry risk. The value of investments can go down as well as up and you may not get back the amount originally invested. Past performance is not a reliable indicator of future results. See our Risk Disclosure for full details.

8. Fees & Charges

Fees applicable to your account and investments are described in our Fees & Charges schedule. By using the Platform, you agree to pay all applicable fees. We may revise our fee schedule with reasonable notice. Management fees are deducted from portfolio performance and disclosed transparently in your dashboard.

9. Platform Availability

We strive to maintain Platform availability 24 hours a day, but we do not guarantee uninterrupted access. The Platform may be unavailable due to maintenance, system updates, or circumstances beyond our control. We are not liable for losses arising from Platform unavailability.

10. Intellectual Property

All content on the Platform — including text, graphics, logos, software, and design elements — is the property of EuroFiducia or its licensors and is protected by intellectual property laws. You may not reproduce, distribute, or create derivative works without our prior written consent.

11. User Conduct

You agree not to: (a) use the Platform for any unlawful purpose; (b) attempt to gain unauthorized access to systems or data; (c) interfere with the proper functioning of the Platform; (d) provide false or misleading information; (e) engage in money laundering, fraud, or any activity prohibited under AML regulations; (f) use automated systems to access the Platform in a manner that sends more requests than a human reasonably could.

12. Limitation of Liability

To the maximum extent permitted by law, EuroFiducia shall not be liable for indirect, incidental, special, consequential, or punitive damages, or for loss of profits, arising from your use of the Platform. Our total liability for any claim shall not exceed the fees you have paid us in the twelve months preceding the claim.

This limitation does not apply to liability that cannot be excluded under applicable law, including liability for gross negligence, willful misconduct, or breach of regulatory obligations.

13. Termination

You may close your account at any time by contacting support, subject to the settlement of all open positions and withdrawal of remaining funds. We may suspend or terminate your account if you breach these Terms, if we are required to do so by law or regulatory authority, or if we suspect fraudulent or suspicious activity.

14. Governing Law & Dispute Resolution

These Terms are governed by French law for French residents and Italian law for Italian residents, with EU regulations applying to cross-border matters. Disputes shall be resolved through negotiation, then mediation, and finally through the courts of your jurisdiction of residence. Consumers may also use the European Online Dispute Resolution platform.

15. Changes to Terms

We may update these Terms from time to time. We will notify you of material changes via email and dashboard message. Continued use of the Platform after changes take effect constitutes acceptance of the revised Terms.

Questions? Our AI support assistant is available 24/7 in your language, or contact our compliance team via the support center. See our Complaints Procedure if you have a dispute.

Privacy Policy

How we collect, use, and protect your personal data

Last updated: January 2024 · GDPR Compliant

Contents

  • 1. Data Controller
  • 2. Data We Collect
  • 3. Legal Basis
  • 4. How We Use Data
  • 5. Data Sharing
  • 6. International Transfers
  • 7. Data Retention
  • 8. Your Rights (GDPR)
  • 9. Security
  • 10. Cookies
  • 11. Children's Privacy
  • 12. Contact & DPO

1. Data Controller

EuroFiducia SAS is the data controller responsible for your personal data within the meaning of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR, Regulation 2016/679) and the French Data Protection Act (Loi Informatique et Libertés) for French residents, and the Italian Privacy Code (Codice della Privacy, D.Lgs. 196/2003 as amended) for Italian residents.

2. Personal Data We Collect

Identity Data

  • Full name, date of birth, nationality
  • Government ID number and document copy
  • Tax identification number (fiscal code / numéro fiscal)

Contact Data

  • Email address, phone number, postal address
  • Preferred language for communications

Financial Data

  • Bank account details (IBAN, BIC)
  • Payment card details (processed by PCI-DSS compliant providers)
  • Transaction history, portfolio holdings, investment profile

Technical Data

  • IP address, browser type, device information
  • Usage data, page visits, login timestamps
  • Cookie data (see our Cookie Policy)

3. Legal Basis for Processing

We process your personal data under the following legal bases:

  • Contract — to open and manage your account and execute your investment instructions.
  • Legal obligation — to comply with AML/KYC regulations, tax reporting, and regulatory requirements.
  • Legitimate interests — to prevent fraud, secure our platform, and improve our services.
  • Consent — for marketing communications, cookies, and optional features, which you may withdraw at any time.

4. How We Use Your Data

  • Account opening, verification (KYC), and ongoing management
  • Processing deposits, withdrawals, and investment transactions
  • Generating transaction receipts and statements
  • Providing AI-powered customer support in your language
  • Notifying administrators of account activity (visits, deposits, withdrawals, support messages) for security and service quality
  • Sending administrative messages to your email and dashboard
  • Complying with legal, regulatory, and tax obligations
  • Preventing fraud, money laundering, and unauthorized access

5. Data Sharing

We do not sell your personal data. We share data only with:

  • Regulatory authorities — AMF (France), CONSOB (Italy), and other competent authorities as required by law.
  • Payment providers — banks and payment processors to execute your transactions.
  • Identity verification providers — for KYC checks.
  • Custodians and depositories — to hold your investments securely.
  • Professional advisors — legal, audit, and tax advisors under confidentiality obligations.

6. International Data Transfers

Your data is primarily processed within the European Economic Area (EEA). Where data is transferred outside the EEA, we ensure appropriate safeguards are in place, such as Standard Contractual Clauses approved by the European Commission, and we comply with GDPR requirements for international transfers.

7. Data Retention

We retain your personal data for as long as your account is active and for the period required by law thereafter. AML/KYC records are retained for a minimum of 5 years after the end of the business relationship, in accordance with AMLD5. Transaction records are retained for 7–10 years as required by tax and regulatory authorities.

8. Your Rights Under GDPR

As a data subject, you have the following rights:

  • Right of access — request a copy of your personal data.
  • Right to rectification — correct inaccurate or incomplete data.
  • Right to erasure — request deletion of your data (subject to legal retention requirements).
  • Right to restrict processing — limit how we use your data.
  • Right to data portability — receive your data in a structured, machine-readable format.
  • Right to object — object to processing based on legitimate interests or for marketing.
  • Right to withdraw consent — at any time for consent-based processing.
  • Right to lodge a complaint — with the CNIL (France) or Garante (Italy).
To exercise any of these rights, contact our Data Protection Officer at privacy@eurofiducia.eu or through your dashboard support center.

9. Data Security

We implement bank-grade security measures including TLS encryption for all data in transit, AES-256 encryption for data at rest, segregated client accounts, multi-factor authentication options, and regular security audits. Access to personal data is restricted to authorized personnel on a need-to-know basis.

10. Cookies

We use cookies to operate the Platform, remember your language preference, and analyze usage. See our Cookie Policy for full details and how to manage cookies.

11. Children's Privacy

The Platform is not directed to individuals under 18. We do not knowingly collect personal data from minors. If you believe we have collected data from a minor, please contact us immediately.

12. Contact & Data Protection Officer

For any privacy-related questions or to exercise your rights, contact:
Data Protection Officer — privacy@eurofiducia.eu
EuroFiducia SAS, Paris, France

You may also lodge a complaint with the CNIL (Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés, France) or the Garante per la protezione dei dati personali (Italy).

Risk Disclosure Statement

Understanding the risks of investing through EuroFiducia

Last updated: January 2024 · MiFID II Compliant
Important: This document provides important information about the risks associated with investing through the EuroFiducia Platform. You should read it carefully before making any investment. By using the Platform, you confirm that you have read and understood these risks.

1. General Investment Risk

All investments carry risk. The value of investments and any income from them can go down as well as up, and you may not get back the amount originally invested. Past performance is not a reliable indicator of future results. No representation or warranty is given as to the achievement of any target return shown on the Platform.

2. Market Risk

Investment values are affected by market movements including changes in equity prices, bond yields, interest rates, currency exchange rates, and commodity prices. Market volatility can cause significant short-term fluctuations in your portfolio value.

3. Specific Product Risks

Stocks & Equities

Equity investments carry the risk of partial or total loss of capital. Individual stocks can become worthless if the issuing company fails. Market sentiment, economic conditions, and company-specific events all affect share prices.

ETFs (Exchange-Traded Funds)

ETFs are subject to the same risks as their underlying assets. Tracking error, liquidity risk, and counterparty risk (for synthetic ETFs) may apply.

Bonds (OAT, BTP)

Bonds carry interest rate risk (bond prices fall when rates rise), credit/default risk (the issuer may fail to pay), and inflation risk. Italian BTPs and French OATs are government bonds subject to sovereign risk.

Real Estate (SCPI)

SCPI investments carry liquidity risk (redemptions may be delayed), property market risk, tenant default risk, and the risk that rental income and capital values may decline.

Sustainable / ESG Funds

ESG funds may have limited investment universes, potentially affecting diversification. ESG criteria and ratings methodologies vary and may change over time.

Private Equity

Private equity is illiquid, with long lock-up periods (typically 7–10 years). Valuations are infrequent and may not reflect realizable values. There is a risk of total capital loss.

Commodities

Commodity prices are highly volatile and affected by supply/demand, geopolitical events, and weather. Commodity investments can experience sharp price movements.

Cryptoassets

Cryptoassets are extremely volatile and high-risk. Prices can fluctuate dramatically. Regulatory treatment varies by jurisdiction and may change. There is a risk of total capital loss. Cryptoassets are not protected by deposit guarantee schemes.

Retirement Products (PER, Pension)

Retirement products typically have long lock-in periods. Early withdrawal may be restricted or subject to penalties and tax consequences. Returns are not guaranteed.

Cash & Savings (Livret A, LDDS)

While low-risk, savings products carry inflation risk — returns may not keep pace with inflation, reducing real purchasing power over time. Interest rates are regulated and may change.

4. Liquidity Risk

Some investments, particularly private equity, SCPI real estate, and certain bonds, may be difficult to sell quickly. You may not be able to access your money when you need it, or you may have to sell at a price below the current valuation.

5. Currency Risk

If you invest in assets denominated in currencies other than the euro, changes in exchange rates may affect the value of your investments. Currency hedging is available for some portfolios but does not eliminate all currency risk.

6. Credit & Counterparty Risk

There is a risk that banks, custodians, or other counterparties may default on their obligations. We use regulated, segregated arrangements to mitigate this, but counterparty risk cannot be entirely eliminated.

7. Regulatory & Tax Risk

Investment regulations and tax treatment may change. Changes in French, Italian, or EU law could affect the value, taxation, or availability of your investments. You are responsible for your own tax obligations.

8. Technology & Cyber Risk

As a digital platform, we are exposed to technology risks including system failures, cyber attacks, and data breaches. We implement extensive security measures, but no system is completely secure. Platform unavailability may prevent you from acting on your investments at critical times.

9. AI Support Risk

Our AI-powered customer support provides general information only and does not constitute investment advice. AI responses may be limited in scope. For complex queries, our AI will escalate to human advisors. Always conduct your own research or consult a qualified financial advisor before investing.

10. Risk Classification

Each portfolio and product on the Platform is assigned a risk rating. Our Conservative portfolios are classified as low risk (1–2 on a 7-point scale), Balanced as medium risk (3–4), and Growth/Euro Growth/Global Growth as medium-high to high risk (5–7). You should select investments appropriate to your risk tolerance, investment objectives, and time horizon as assessed during registration.

11. No Advice

EuroFiducia provides an execution-only platform. We do not provide personalized investment advice. The portfolio descriptions and target returns are illustrative. You are responsible for your investment decisions. If you need advice, consult an authorized financial advisor.

Need help understanding risk? Our AI support can explain product risks in your language, or contact our team via the support center for a human advisor.

AML & KYC Policy

Anti-Money Laundering and Know Your Customer procedures

Last updated: January 2024 · AMLD5/AMLD6 Compliant

1. Overview

EuroFiducia is committed to preventing money laundering, terrorist financing, and financial crime. We comply with the EU Anti-Money Laundering Directives (AMLD5, Directive 2018/843 and AMLD6, Directive 2018/1673), the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), and Italian Legislative Decree 231/2007 as amended.

2. Know Your Customer (KYC)

Before activating your account, we are required to verify your identity. Our KYC process includes:

  • Identity verification — Full name, date of birth, nationality, and a valid government-issued photo ID (passport, national ID card, or driving licence for EU residents).
  • Address verification — Proof of residential address (utility bill, bank statement, or official document dated within the last 3 months).
  • Tax identification — Your tax identification number (numéro fiscal in France, codice fiscale in Italy) for reporting and compliance purposes.
  • Source of funds — Information about the origin of funds you intend to invest.

3. Customer Due Diligence (CDD)

We apply risk-based customer due diligence to all clients:

  • Simplified due diligence — For low-risk clients and certain regulated products.
  • Standard due diligence — Identity and address verification, source of funds confirmation.
  • Enhanced due diligence (EDD) — For high-risk clients, including PEPs (Politically Exposed Persons), clients from high-risk jurisdictions, or complex/large transactions. EDD requires senior management approval and additional documentation.

4. Politically Exposed Persons (PEP)

During registration, you are required to declare whether you are a PEP, a family member of a PEP, or a known close associate of a PEP. PEPs are individuals who hold or have held prominent public functions. If you are a PEP, we will apply enhanced due diligence and obtain senior management approval before establishing the business relationship.

5. Sanctions Screening

We screen all clients against EU, UN, OFAC, and national sanctions lists at onboarding and on an ongoing basis. Accounts matching sanctions lists will be blocked and reported to the relevant authorities. We also screen against lists of known terrorists and financial criminals.

6. Transaction Monitoring

We monitor transactions for suspicious activity using automated and manual processes. Red flags include:

  • Unusual transaction patterns inconsistent with the client's profile
  • Large or frequent cash deposits without clear economic purpose
  • Structuring transactions to avoid reporting thresholds
  • Transfers to or from high-risk jurisdictions
  • Sudden changes in investment behavior inconsistent with the client's stated objectives

Suspicious transactions are investigated by our compliance team and, where appropriate, reported to TRACFIN (France) or UIF (Unità di Informazione Finanziaria, Italy) — the national financial intelligence units.

7. Reporting Obligations

Under AML regulations, we are required to report suspicious activities to the relevant financial intelligence unit. Such reports are confidential, and we are prohibited from informing clients that a report has been made (this is known as "tipping off" and is a criminal offense).

8. Record Keeping

We retain KYC documentation, transaction records, and compliance documentation for a minimum of 5 years after the end of the business relationship, in accordance with AMLD5. Certain records may be retained longer where required by other regulatory or tax obligations.

9. Client Obligations

As a client, you agree to:

  • Provide accurate, complete, and truthful information during onboarding and ongoing
  • Inform us of any changes to your personal details, address, or tax status
  • Cooperate with any additional verification requests
  • Not use the Platform for money laundering, terrorist financing, or any unlawful purpose
  • Understand that we may delay or refuse transactions that trigger compliance concerns

10. Consequences of Non-Compliance

If we cannot verify your identity, or if we identify suspicious activity, we may:

  • Delay or refuse to execute transactions
  • Suspend or close your account
  • Report to the relevant financial intelligence unit
  • Cooperate fully with regulatory and law enforcement authorities

11. Training & Governance

All EuroFiducia employees receive regular AML/KYC training. Our compliance program is overseen by a designated Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) and reviewed by senior management and external auditors.

12. Contact

For AML/KYC questions, contact our Compliance Department at compliance@eurofiducia.eu or through your dashboard support center.

Your privacy matters: AML/KYC data is handled under strict confidentiality and GDPR compliance. See our Privacy Policy for details on how your data is protected.

Cookie Policy

How and why we use cookies on the EuroFiducia Platform

Last updated: January 2024

1. What Are Cookies?

Cookies are small text files placed on your device when you visit a website. They allow the site to remember your actions and preferences over a period of time, so you don't have to re-enter them every time you visit. Cookies are widely used to make websites work efficiently and to provide information to site owners.

2. Types of Cookies We Use

Essential Cookies

These cookies are necessary for the Platform to function. They enable core functionality such as security, session management, and account access. Without these cookies, the Platform cannot operate properly.

  • Session cookie — keeps you logged in during your visit.
  • Security cookie — protects against fraudulent access.
  • Language cookie — remembers your preferred language (French, Italian, etc.).

Functional Cookies

These cookies enable enhanced functionality and personalization, such as remembering your dashboard preferences and investment watchlist.

Analytics Cookies

These cookies help us understand how visitors interact with the Platform so we can improve its performance and user experience. We track aggregated, anonymized visit data, which also generates notifications to our administrative team about Platform activity.

Preference Cookies

These cookies remember your settings and choices, such as your selected risk profile display and regional portfolio preferences.

3. Managing Cookies

You can control and manage cookies through your browser settings. Most browsers allow you to refuse cookies or alert you when cookies are being sent. Please note that disabling essential cookies may affect Platform functionality and prevent you from logging in or completing transactions.

  • Chrome — Settings → Privacy and security → Cookies
  • Firefox — Settings → Privacy & Security → Cookies
  • Safari — Preferences → Privacy → Cookies
  • Edge — Settings → Cookies and site permissions

4. Third-Party Cookies

In some cases, we may use third-party services that set cookies. These include payment processors (for transaction security), identity verification providers (for KYC), and analytics providers. These third parties manage cookies according to their own privacy policies.

5. Updates to This Policy

We may update this Cookie Policy from time to time. We will notify you of significant changes via the Platform or email. Continued use of the Platform after changes take effect constitutes acceptance of the updated policy.

6. Contact Us

For questions about our use of cookies, contact us at privacy@eurofiducia.eu or through your dashboard support center.

Complaints Procedure

How to make a complaint and how we handle it

Last updated: January 2024 · France & Italy
Our commitment: We take every complaint seriously. You can submit a complaint in your language, and we will respond in your language. All complaints are handled free of charge.

1. How to Make a Complaint

If you have a complaint about our services, you can contact us through any of the following channels:

  • Dashboard Support Center — Use the support chat in your dashboard. Our AI assistant will handle common issues, and escalate to human advisors when needed. All support messages are tracked with a ticket number.
  • Email — complaints@eurofiducia.eu
  • Postal address — EuroFiducia SAS, Complaints Department, Paris, France

Please provide: your full name, account number, a clear description of your complaint, and any relevant reference numbers (such as transaction IDs from your receipts).

2. Complaint Handling Process

Step 1: Acknowledgment (within 2 business days)

We will acknowledge receipt of your complaint within 2 business days and assign you a unique reference number. You will receive this acknowledgment in your language via email and dashboard message.

Step 2: Investigation (within 15 business days)

Your complaint will be investigated by our Client Relations team. We aim to provide a full response within 15 business days. If the investigation requires more time, we will inform you of the expected timeframe.

Step 3: Resolution

We will provide a written response detailing our findings, any remedial action, and your options if you remain dissatisfied. Responses are provided in your language.

3. Escalation Within EuroFiducia

If you are not satisfied with the initial response, you may request escalation to our Head of Compliance, who will conduct an independent review. This should be requested within 30 days of receiving our initial response.

4. External Dispute Resolution

If your complaint is not resolved to your satisfaction, you have the right to escalate to the relevant external dispute resolution body:

For French Residents 🇫🇷

  • AMF Médiateur — The Ombudsman of the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF). You may submit a complaint to the AMF Mediator after exhausting our internal procedure.
  • Website: www.amf-france.org
  • The AMF Mediator can be contacted for disputes that remain unresolved after our internal process.

For Italian Residents 🇮🇹

  • CONSOB / ABI Conciliatore Bancario — For investment disputes, you may contact the CONSOB or the Banking Conciliator ( Conciliatore Bancario Paritetico).
  • Website: www.consob.it · www.conciliatorebancario.it
  • Italian law provides for alternative dispute resolution through the Arbitro Bancario Finanziario (ABF).

European ODR Platform

Consumers may also use the European Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) platform at ec.europa.eu/consumers/odr for cross-border disputes.

5. Time Limits

Please submit complaints as soon as possible. Under applicable regulations, complaints should be submitted within a reasonable time of the event giving rise to the complaint. We may decline to investigate complaints about events more than 12 months old, unless there are exceptional circumstances.

6. Confidentiality

All complaints are handled confidentially. Information you provide will be used only for investigating your complaint and will be shared only with personnel directly involved in the investigation.

7. No Retaliation

You will not be disadvantaged in any way for making a complaint in good faith. We value feedback as an opportunity to improve our services.

8. Contact

Complaints Department
Email: complaints@eurofiducia.eu

Regulatory Information

Our regulatory status and authorizations

Last updated: January 2024
Important: This is a demonstration platform. EuroFiducia is a fictional company created for illustrative purposes. It is not a real regulated entity and does not hold any actual regulatory authorizations.

1. Company Information

EuroFiducia SAS is a simplified joint-stock company (société par actions simplifiée) registered in Paris, France, providing cross-border digital investment services to residents of France and Italy and other eligible European jurisdictions.

  • Registered office: Paris, France
  • Italian office: Milan, Italy
  • Legal form: SAS (France) / Sede secondaria (Italy)
  • VAT/Tax ID: FR 00 000000000 (illustrative)
  • Share capital: €5,000,000

2. Regulatory Framework

EuroFiducia operates within the European Union's financial regulatory framework, including:

  • MiFID II — Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (Directive 2014/65/EU)
  • AMLD5/AMLD6 — Anti-Money Laundering Directives
  • GDPR — General Data Protection Regulation (Regulation 2016/679)
  • UCITS / AIFMD — Undertakings for Collective Investment / Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive
  • EMIR — European Market Infrastructure Regulation
  • DORA — Digital Operational Resilience Act

3. French Regulation

Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF)

The AMF is the French financial markets regulator, responsible for protecting investors and ensuring orderly financial markets. EuroFiducia's activities in France fall under AMF supervision in accordance with the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier).

  • AMF — 17 place de la Bourse, 75002 Paris, France
  • Website: www.amf-france.org
  • AMF Grieco number: [illustrative]

ACPR

The Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution (ACPR) supervises banks and insurance companies in France and ensures financial stability. EuroFiducia's banking relationships and payment services are subject to ACPR oversight.

Banque de France

The Banque de France, France's central bank, oversees monetary policy and financial stability. French regulated savings products (Livret A, LDDS) are governed by the Banque de France and the French state.

4. Italian Regulation

CONSOB

The Commissione Nazionale per le Società e la Borsa (CONSOB) is Italy's financial markets regulator, ensuring transparency and investor protection. EuroFiducia's activities in Italy fall under CONSOB supervision in accordance with Italian financial law (Testo Unico della Finanza, D.Lgs. 58/1998).

  • CONSOB — Via Giovanni Battista Martini, 3, 00198 Roma, Italy
  • Website: www.consob.it

Banca d'Italia

The Banca d'Italia, Italy's central bank, supervises banking and payment services. Italian government bonds (BTP, BOT) and savings products are governed under Banca d'Italia oversight.

Guardia di Finanza & UIF

The Unità di Informazione Finanziaria (UIF), hosted at Banca d'Italia, is Italy's financial intelligence unit responsible for AML supervision. Suspicious activity reports are submitted to the UIF for Italian operations.

5. Investor Protection

French Investors

Client assets are held in segregated accounts separate from EuroFiducia's own funds. In the event of EuroFiducia's failure, the Fonds de Garantie des Dépôts et de Résolution (FGDR) provides deposit guarantee coverage up to €100,000 per depositor per institution, subject to conditions.

Italian Investors

Italian investor protection is provided through the Fondo Nazionale di Garanzia (National Guarantee Fund), which covers deposits up to €100,000 per depositor per bank, in accordance with EU Directive 2014/49/EU.

6. Cross-Border Passporting

Under MiFID II, EuroFiducia provides services across EU member states under a passporting regime. Our services to Italian residents are provided under the EU single-market passport, with notification to CONSOB as required.

7. Best Execution

EuroFiducia is committed to achieving the best possible result for client orders. Our order execution policy takes into account price, cost, speed, likelihood of execution and settlement, size, and nature of the order. We monitor execution quality and review our venues regularly.

8. Conflicts of Interest

We maintain a conflicts of interest policy to identify, prevent, and manage conflicts that may arise between EuroFiducia and our clients. Where a conflict cannot be avoided, we disclose its nature to affected clients before acting.

9. Complaints & Redress

For information on how to make a complaint and available redress mechanisms, see our Complaints Procedure.

10. Disclaimer

This Regulatory Information page is provided for transparency and educational purposes. EuroFiducia is a demonstration platform and does not hold actual regulatory authorizations. No real financial services are provided. This page illustrates how a regulated European investment platform would present its regulatory status.
